Checked deterministic encoding, collision disposition, replay idempotence, A-to-B-to-A preservation, and distinct load/effective axes.

invariant_checking.notes: The invariants preserve retained canonical inputs/provenance so hashes never become the sole evidence of identity or payload equality.

evidence: Reviewed set-algebra proof that a deterministic distinct anti-join inserts no keys on exact replay after the first atomic insertion.
Reviewed maximal-run argument that first-of-run retention is necessary and sufficient to represent every consecutive payload transition.
Verified that digest equality assumptions and collision controls limit both arguments appropriately.
proof_review.notes: The proofs establish set replay and transition compression only; they do not prove business-key quality, source correctness, or universal collision absence.

evidence: The history argument is explicitly labeled run-compression proof sketch and states the collision-free equality assumption.
The hub set result is labeled a proof and its deterministic-canonicalization and atomic-uniqueness assumptions are adjacent.
The collision equation is labeled a birthday approximation rather than a uniqueness theorem.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Formal, approximate, invariant, and implementation-observation claims are differentiated consistently.

evidence: The executable example demonstrates a finite deterministic loader without claiming production completeness.
The empirical evidence boundary says tested fixtures cannot prove business-key stability, cross-source identity, or universal collision absence.
Operational recommendations require replay, shuffled-order, cross-platform canonicalization, collision, and mart reconciliation tests.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Observed tool behavior and architectural/methodological claims are clearly separated.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed fit criteria, architecture versus table patterns, business concepts/scoped keys, hub/link/satellite grains, relationship effectivity, multi-active states, two time axes, provenance, hashes/hashdiffs, Raw/Business Vault boundaries, PIT/bridge assistance, marts, automation, and evolution. practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable guidance for canonical serialization, parallel and concurrent loads, source-specific satellites, late records, deletion inference, corrections, metadata generation, reconciliation, collision detection, consistent publication, recovery, access/erasure, and delivery-layer performance. Adversarial fixtures address production failure modes.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review establishes vocabulary and invariants; exposition progresses from fit and business modeling through loading, history, delivery and operations; notation supports proofs; the executable example is reproducible; ten worked examples are distinct; and five exercises with complete answers cover design, canonicalization, ordering, loading and delivery.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Sources and local execution were checked on 2026-09-02, but proprietary certification material, organization-specific methodology decisions, production-scale collision/performance evidence, and future tool behavior remain outside this review.
